stances.claim: Beyond the suffragists, many Filipina power women have excelled in private professions, achieving equality if not superiority with men.
stances.rhetorical_move: broadened-recognition thesis prompted by reader response

stances.claim: Bernadine Siy is the first lady chairperson of both ADMU and the Manila Golf Club -- the latter a 'bastion of masculine pride' since 1901 -- and is listened to with respect and awe in the boardrooms of PLDT and JG Summit.
Marife Zamora is the first lady president of the MAP and the founder of the Filipina CEO Circle.
Charo Santos's distinction extends beyond film: she was the first lady president/CEO of ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp. (2008-2015), magnificently bringing it to its peak in revenues and reach.
Vilma Santos reinvented herself successfully in politics -- Lipa mayor, Batangas governor, and Batangas congressional representative -- while keeping her movie allure.

notable_anecdotes: Author teasing Fr. Bobby Yap that though women cannot be priests, the Jesuits installed a lady (Bern Siy) as their ADMU board chair -- Yap always smiling in agreement.
MGC's 1901 founding as a 'bastion of masculine pride' until the 1987 glass ceiling break and Bern Siy's election as its first lady president in 2008.
Lilia de Lima breaking the MAP record by becoming the first female Management Man of the Year (2010) and later receiving the Ramon Magsaysay Award (2017).
Korina Sanchez-Roxas's Bilyonaryo podcast with Mike Toledo and Pinky Webb reportedly drawing 500,000 views.
Charo Santos's 1978 Itim winning best picture at the Asean Film Festival with her named best actress, capped by her 2008-2015 stewardship of ABS-CBN.
Gina Pareño winning best actress in Belgium, India, and France for her lead role in Kubrador, produced by Joji Alonso.

one_paragraph_summary: Following reader responses to his Woman Suffrage Day column urging recognition of women's excellence beyond the suffrage struggle, Panganiban honors the 'power women' of the Philippines in the private professions. He leads with Bernadine 'Bern' Siy, the first lady chairperson of Ateneo de Manila University and of the Manila Golf Club (a 1901-founded 'bastion of masculine pride' until the 1987 glass ceiling break and Siy's 2008 election as its first lady president), and his fellow independent director at PLDT and JG Summit. He profiles Marife Zamora, first lady president of the Management Association of the Philippines and founder of the Filipina CEO Circle, and Dr. Lydia B. Echauz, an ID across Meralco, SPNEC, Shell, and D&L Industries and former president of FEU and dean of DLSU Graduate School. He lists power lady executives -- Chaye Cabal-Revilla (MPIC), Martha Sazon (GCash), Meean Dy (Ayala Land), Lynette Ortiz (Land Bank), Rhoda Huang (Filinvest), Lourdes Gutierrez-Alfonso (Megaworld), Hannah Yulo-Luccini (Hotel101 Global), Lorelie Quiambao-Osial (Shell), Riena Pama (Sun Life Prosperity Fund), and Sandy Prieto-Romualdez (Inquirer Group) -- and notes Lilia de Lima's distinction as the first female Management Man of the Year (2010) and 2017 Ramon Magsaysay awardee. He extends the honor roll alphabetically across broadcast (Arcangel, Constantino, Cosim, Cruz-Valdes, Davila, Drilon, Jacob-Sandejas, Lazaro, Morales-Reyno, Ressa, Sanchez-Roxas, Sembrano, Soho, Tiangco), music and performing arts led by Lea Salonga (Constantino, Cuneta, Dela Torre, Gerodias, Geronimo-Guidicelli, Go, Ledesma, Legaspi-Gallardo, Macuja-Elizalde, Misalucha, San Jose, Velasquez-Alcasid, Zobel-Elizalde), and a film-industry living-legends list submitted by Joji Alonso (Guillen, Gil, Koronel, Pareño, Roa Rodrigo, Rodriguez, Sanchez, Santos, Santos, Villa). He highlights Charo Santos's twin achievements -- 1978 Asean Film Festival best picture and best actress for Itim, and stewardship of ABS-CBN as its first lady president/CEO (2008-2015) -- Vilma Santos's political reinvention as Lipa mayor, Batangas governor, and congresswoman, and Gina Pareño's international best-actress awards in Belgium, India, and France for Kubrador.
